glosses: to inform, to notify (to give (someone) notice of (something))
To instruct, train (usually in matters of knowledge).

examples.text: For he would learn their business secretly, / And then inform his master hastily.
I am informed thoroughly of the cause.

glosses: To act as an informer; denounce.
To give form or character to; to inspire (with a given quality); to affect, influence (with a pervading principle, idea etc.).

examples.text: His sense of religion informs everything he writes.

WikiLeaks did not cause these uprisings but it certainly informed them. The dispatches revealed details of corruption and kleptocracy that many Tunisians suspected, but could not prove, and would cite as they took to the streets.
Let others better mould the running mass / Of metals, and inform the breathing brass
O! long as breath informs this fleeting frame / Ne'er let me pass in silence Dorset's name

glosses: To make known, wisely and/or knowledgeably.

examples.text: Don't forget the code of ethics that informs this profession.

glosses: To take form; to become visible or manifest; to appear.

examples.text: It is the bloody business which informs / Thus to mine eyes.

glosses: Without regular form; shapeless; ugly; deformed.

examples.text:
Bleak Crags, and naked Hills,
And the whole Prospect so inform and rude
The dispatcher immediately notified the volunteer fire department of the emergency call.
Once a decision has been reached and notified to the parties it becomes binding.
He took no notice of the changes, and went on as though nothing had happened.

Athelstan Arundel walked home[…], foaming and raging. […] He walked the whole way, walking through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.
How ready is envy to mingle with the notices which we take of other persons?
Shall we post a notice about the new policy?
A notice was attached to the building reminding the residents about the five hour water shortage that was happening today.
I always read the death notices in the paper.
The sidewalk adjacent to the damaged bridge stonework shall be closed until further notice.

glosses: Advance notification of termination of employment, given by an employer to an employee or vice versa.

examples.text: I gave her her mandatory two weeks' notice and sacked her.
I can't work here any longer. I'm giving notice.

glosses: A published critical review of a play or the like.

examples.text: The first-night audience, yes. The first-night reviewers, not exactly. The notices have so far been mixed, only The Financial Times having delivered itself of an unequivocal rave.
I don't mind if you want to change the venue; just give me some notice first, OK?
I have been with your father and given him notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his duchess will be here with him this night.
Numberless are the arguments […] that men have used morally and physically, to degrade the sex. I must notice a few.

glosses: To become aware of; to observe.

examples.text: Did you notice the flowers in her yard?
So you punched out a window for ventilation. Was that before or after you noticed you were standing in a lake of gasoline?

[The researchers] noticed many of their pieces of [plastic marine] debris sported surface pits around two microns across. Such pits are about the size of a bacterial cell. Closer examination showed that some of these pits did, indeed, contain bacteria, […].

glosses: To lavish attention upon; to treat (someone) favourably.

examples.text: She would notice her; she would improve her; she would detach her from her bad acquaintance, and introduce her into good society; she would form her opinions and her manners.
The blackness didn't notice so much when she was born; but it's unmistakeable now.

glosses: jemanden von etwas in Kenntnis setzen, jemandem eine Nachricht zukommen lassen

examples.text: Der Mitarbeiter wurde über die Kündigung benachrichtigt.
Das Krankenhaus benachrichtigte sofort nach dem Tod seine Ehefrau.
„Die Mutter einer Schizophrenen benachrichtigte den behandelnden Psychiater telefonisch, dass der Zustand ihrer Tochter sich wieder verschlechterte.“
„Da hat meine Mutter zwei alte deutsche Schulbücher gefunden, daraus unterrichtet sie mich in Erdkunde und Geschichte.“
„Viele gut ausgebildete Lehrkräfte unterrichten lieber in gutbürgerlichen Stadtteilen“, sagt [der Bildungsforscher Klaus] Klemm.
„Die Mutter ist Lehrerin und unterrichtet ihre Kinder bis zum Abitur.“
„Männer fehlen in Kindergärten, aber auch in Grundschulen, wo zu mehr als 85 Prozent Frauen unterrichten.“
Die Arbeitsgruppe unterrichtete das Plenum über die Beratungsergebnisse.
Er teilte Peter mit, dass er in den Besprechungsraum kommen soll.
„Außerdem hatte ich ihm in einem meiner Briefe mitgeteilt, dass ich das Chemiestudium zwar zu Ende führen würde, aber dann lieber Schriftsteller werden wolle.“
„Die Täter rückten am Sonntag in den Morgenstunden mit einem Radlader an und durchbrachen damit die Außenwand einer Bankfiliale in Mellingen bei Weimar, wie die Polizei mitteilte.“
„Der Klettersport erschließt mir die Möglichkeit, mich meiner Umwelt mitzuteilen und Kontakt herzustellen. Der Fels ist dabei mein Freund.“
